t: Cross-Domain Discovery Engine: a plain-language overview
title: Cross-Domain Discovery Engine: a plain-language overview
description: Overview: what the Cross-Domain Discovery Engine does and why archives need it. A cross-domain discovery engine hunts for ideas that work in one field and could work in another: the way ants find food inspiring delivery routes, or the way epidemics spread modeling how rumors spread. It maps the shared structure between fields and proposes the transfer. Separate sciences start talking to each other.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Cross-Domain Discovery Engine works
title: How the Cross-Domain Discovery Engine works
description: Overview: what the Cross-Domain Discovery Engine does and why archives need it. Real discovery engines represent each domain's concepts and relations as graphs, then search for structural analogies — matching relational patterns (A flows to B through C) across domains with different surface terms. Bipartite mapping aligns concepts by role similarity, and candidate transfers are scored by structural fidelity plus evidence that the mechanism is domain-independent. Each proposal cites the source analogy, the mapped structure, and the transfer hypothesis.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Cross-Domain Discovery Engine works: the deep tour
title: How the Cross-Domain Discovery Engine works: the deep tour
description: Overview: what the Cross-Domain Discovery Engine does and why archives need it. Real discovery engines represent each domain's concepts and relations as graphs, then search for structural analogies — matching relational patterns (A flows to B through C) across domains with different surface terms. Bipartite mapping aligns concepts by role similarity, and candidate transfers are scored by structural fidelity plus evidence that the mechanism is domain-independent. Each proposal cites the source analogy, the mapped structure, and the transfer hypothesis. Advanced systems use embedding spaces trained across domains, validate transfers against known successful crossovers (simulated annealing from metallurgy to optimization), and flag superficial analogies that share words but not structure. Quality is measured by expert ratings of proposed transfers. The limits are analogies that inspire but do not transfer — the engine proposes hypotheses for testing, never claiming a transfer works before it is tried, because a pretty analogy is not a proof.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.
